_meta.description: The SIMPLE structure profile, and the default one (openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-10-simple-structure-profile). `menu-layout.json` is the FULL profile and is untouched: an administrator brings it back with the setting `menu_structure`. Both profiles are built from the same manifest and the same fragments, so nothing is deleted and every page stays routable; this file only decides what the navigation offers first. THE FOUR STANDARD KEYS (`relocations`, `removals`, `settingsSection`, `integrationsSection`) go to the library's buildManifest exactly as the full file's do. `relocations` is absent because nothing moves: the simple menu is flat, eight entries, the first group without a caption and the others under one each, as DqZijbalk draws them, plus the case types each user chose under My case types. The library's relocation step keeps a caption unless the relocations emptied it, so adding the key would not cost the captions. THE TWO PROFILE KEYS are read by src/utils/structureProfile.js, because buildManifest's layout has no word for either. `menu` is merged BEFORE the manifest's own menu. buildManifest merges entries by id and the FIRST definition of a key wins, so an entry here that carries only `id` and `order` takes its label, icon and route from the manifest and keeps the order written here, and an entry the manifest does not know (the three captions) is simply added. `pages` holds page overlays: `configAppend` appends items to a list in the page's config, by key. It is how My work and the dashboard gain the links that replace the three entries this profile takes out of the menu. A link, not a waiver: tests/vitest/structureProfile.spec.js fails when an entry is removed here and no reachable page links to its route.
_meta.removalsNote: The first eight are the full profile's own removals, repeated because buildManifest takes ONE list; the spec fails when the two drift. The last three are this profile's: `PersonalQueueMenu` (Your queue) and `MyWork` (Assigned to me) are reached from the My work page, and `EndOfDayMenu` (Close out your day) from My work and from the dashboard. `SettingsGroup` is an empty shell in the manifest (a label and no route). The full profile loses it to the relocation step's clean-up; this profile has no relocation step, so it is removed by name.
_meta.settingsNote: The first six are the full profile's. `CasesDeletedMenu`, `CaseObjectsMenu`, `MailIntakeLogMenu` and `WooReportsMenu` join them here: a recycle bin, an object register, an intake log and the Woo review reports are set-up and inspection, not daily work. `WooReportsMenu` shows only to the throughput reader group.
_meta.myCaseTypesNote: The case types a user pins are views of the case list (case-type-pins-are-views): the library's My views section at the bottom of the menu lists them, so this profile has no My case types heading of its own. The backend `/api/manifest` delta adds one view per pinned case type to the Cases page.
_meta.footerNote: The footer keeps Reports, Documentation, Store and Features & roadmap. The library's navigation has no help menu to move them under (nextcloud-vue development, 2026-10-05: CnAppNav renders main, footer and settings, and `actionsMenu.showHelpLinks` belongs to a detail page).

pages._note: The landing page in the simple structure (openspec/changes/landing-views). It carries what the dashboard carried in this structure until 7 October 2026: the greeting with its My work / My team switch, First today, four counts of MY cases, the week, my cases per step, my tasks and continue working (openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-10-simple-list-and-dashboard, whose notes on each widget still hold). THE SWITCH NOW CHANGES VIEWS, NOT PAGES. Its options carry `view` (nextcloud-vue 2.66.0 page views): My work is the `mine` view, My team the `team` view the manifest declares on this page. Before, My work opened the dashboard and My team the team queue, two pages with two headers, and the greeting stood over an empty area. THE GREETING IS THE PAGE'S OWN GRID, the views are drawn below it. `configPatch` replaces only the `mine` view's widgets and layout, so `team` stays the manifest's, one definition for both structures. `mine` keeps two widgets of the full My work page that nothing in the design replaces: Cases you follow and My archival reviews. Deadlines, Open Cases and the task table are not repeated: the week, the counts, First today and My tasks already show the same cases. THE PAGE HEADER STAYS. The dashboard hid it (`showHeader: false`), but this page's header carries the links that stand in for the menu entries this profile removes (Your queue, Assigned to me, Close out your day), and a hidden header hides them too. `simple-my-tasks` is a custom widget, so the page gains its slot.

pages._note: The case page in the simple structure (openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-10-simple-case-page). The full structure has no overlay, so its page is today's page. STAGE: `statusRole` is the role of the status the case sits in (statusType.role), materialised on the case. A status without a role leaves it empty: no what-now card, no stage button, and Lifecycle stays the first entry of the More menu, as it is today. THREE STEPS OF THE DESIGN HAVE NO ACTION OF THEIR OWN IN DOSSIQ and are not invented here: recording a decision (decidiq owns it), publishing as a step (Publish exists, and hangs on wooPublicationStatus, not on a role) and closing as one act (it is a choice inside the Lifecycle dialog). All three open the Lifecycle dialog under the label Next step. THE PILL ABOVE THE TITLE IS THE CASE NUMBER, in the `typePill` place: the case holds its case type as a uuid and no name, so there is no type to show there, and the number is what a handler looks for first. NO COUNTS ON TABS: the case carries no count of its documents, messages or tasks. THE SIX SIDEBAR TABS STAY IN THE SIDEBAR: they are sidebar components, and the tab strip holds widgets. `case-rebind` IS IN THE CASE GROUP AND NOT ADMIN ONLY: who may change a case's type is decided by its own permission endpoint (`mayRebind`), in both structures. The simple structure regroups actions. It does not change who may do what. The same rule keeps `case-version-move` and `cross-domain-lookup` in the Case group: the design lists both as admin actions, but today any handler may use them, and `adminOnly` would take them away. Only the two inspect actions are admin only, and both were already gated on the admin probe. EVERY STAGE WITH A CARD HAS A BUTTON THAT CANNOT HIDE. The intake stage first pointed at Claim, and Claim hides once the case has a handler: a case in intake with a handler showed a finished checklist and no button (live check, 5 October 2026). The library's fallback for a hidden stage action is the page's `primaryAction`, which is a link and cannot open a dialog, so the stage itself names Next step, which opens the Lifecycle dialog and has no condition. Claim stays in the Case group. Waiting for information keeps Remind, whose only condition is that the case is not archived. THREE TILES LEFT THE GRID: beside the side column the grid is narrow and drew number, type and deadline as three full-width cards. The number is the pill, the deadline is the first card of the side column, and the type is in the Overview tab. Hours booked takes the full row. THE HEADER IS A CARD THAT HOLDS THE STAGES (`headerCard`, `headerWidget: case-stages`, nextcloud-vue 2.65.0), so the stages leave the grid. THE BANNER STACK (favourite, follow, new since you looked, what this status asks, attention) moves to the bottom of the side column: DqZaak draws nothing between the header and the tabs, and the column keeps every one of those controls in reach.

NO CREATE (a-delivered-set-is-written-by-publishing-only): a delivered set is what the publish wrote, with the hash of every item, so a hand-made one is a record of a delivery that never happened. The library offered its default Add here, which opened the raw schema form asking a Woo coordinator for a SHA-256 hash and a state (13 October). This section is the declaration, and `hideEmpty` is ON because most cases are handled here and an empty block on every one of them would be noise. What it must never become is a place to record work: the lifecycle acts on such a case come back disabled from CaseActionProvider, naming the application, and execute() refuses the same move rather than trusting the flag.

widgets.title: Receipt confirmation
widgets._note: ontvangstbevestiging REQ-TERM-023 and REQ-TERM-024: whether this case confirmed receipt under Awb 4:3a, when, to whom and by which channel, and the messages it sent on its own. It sits in Communication rather than Data because it IS correspondence, beside the contact a handler logs by hand. A `data` widget and not a bespoke component: both fields are declared on the case schema, so the library renders them from the schema and this change adds no widget to the custom-widget ratchet. Read-only throughout: the duty is written by the acknowledgement service and cleared through the Record receipt confirmed action, never by typing over the field, because a duty a handler can edit silently is the state this feature exists to make visible.

widgets.title: Live conversation
widgets._note: A conversation held live from this case, in Nextcloud Talk, and what the case recorded of the ones already held: the moment, who joined and how long it lasted. It sits in Communication rather than in a tab of its own because a handler reading what was said on this case is already here, and a call and a contact moment are the same question asked of two moments. Rendered by TYPE (case-conversations-pane in registry.js): a section child resolves from the widget registry, and a component registered only by name draws an empty panel and logs nothing. The icon is PhoneInTalk, which src/icons.js carries; an icon a manifest names but no registry holds renders the default glyph and breaks nothing visibly, which is how that goes unnoticed.

widgets.title: Contact moments in the customer record
widgets._note: parties-and-contact-moments-consume-pipelinq 2.2 and 2.3, board DqZaakContactmomenten: pipelinq's contact moments read by MEMBERSHIP of this case, with the line saying a moment is also on other cases (a case the reader may not open counted, not named), and the two filing acts. It sits under dossiq's own Communication list rather than replacing it, because that list is dossiq's record and the one an instance without pipelinq has; this section says in words when pipelinq is absent. Rendered by TYPE (registry key case-pipelinq-contact-moments), as a section child resolves from the registry and an unknown type draws nothing.

widgets.title: Tasks on this case
widgets._note: task-on-the-case A06: the Tasks tab shows the first OPEN task of this case with the lifecycle buttons OpenRegister answers for it, confirms a completion with a toast and puts the next open task in its place, so a handler finishes a task without leaving the case. The id, the title, the icon and the tab entry are unchanged, and no page is added or retyped, so the ADR-100 page ratchet does not move. TYPE is the interim. [blocked: nextcloud-vue 2.41.1 CnObjectListWidget has no rowActions and no lifecycle column] so a button cannot be put inside a row from configuration; verified against the installed 2.40.0 dist and the published 2.41.1 tarball. TARGET: back to type object-list with a lifecycle column (asked for in https://github.com/ConductionNL/nextcloud-vue/issues/1033), at which point src/components/tasks/CaseTaskPane.vue and its registry entry are deleted. The type names the registry key rather than "custom" because this widget is a child of the case-panels tabs widget: CnDetailPage renders a widget-<id> page slot per GRID item only, and CnTabsWidget resolves a tab child through cnRegistry[widget.type], rendering nothing at all when no key answers. content.columns, content.rowRoute and content.emptyText are kept as written: they are what the widget goes back to reading the day the library grows the column. `register` and `schema` are NOT kept, and that is remove-casetask 4.2: the component reads the task engine and has ignored both keys since dossiq#2357, so the pair named a schema that no longer exists and claimed a binding the widget does not make. The day the swap back happens, the list the widget goes back to is the engine's, not an object list, so neither key comes back.

widgets.title: What comes next
widgets._note: task-dependencies-and-the-next-planned-action, gap register row 3.28. A case answers what happens next WITHOUT anybody reading the history, which is the whole reason the record exists. It sits beside Tasks rather than inside it because the two answer different questions: a task is work somebody is doing now, a planned action is work the case type says comes next and that nobody has started. The filter keeps `state: planned` and the sort is `plannedFor` ascending, so the FIRST ROW IS THE ANSWER; completed actions stay readable through the case's own object list rather than crowding the one sentence this section exists to say. `plannedFrom` is a column on purpose: it is what makes a chain readable backwards, so a handler can see that this call was planned by the confirmation before it rather than by somebody typing a date. Rows carry no `rowRoute`: there is no plannedAction detail page, and a route naming a page that does not exist pushes vue-router at a name it cannot resolve.

content.emptyText: No next action is planned on this case

widgets.title: Incidents
widgets._note: splitting-a-case-and-its-incidents REQ-CM-53. Several dated reports inside one case, which is how repeat reports on one address are handled: the case holds the address and the history, and each report is a record with its own reporter, its own owner and its own outcome. SORTED BY `eventDate` AND NOT BY THE RECORDING MOMENT (D-6): a report written up three weeks late belongs where it happened, and `createdAt` order would quietly rewrite the sequence the case is about. It sits in the Work tab rather than in a tab of its own, because the strip is already eleven entries and an incident is work on the case; `recordedAt` is a column beside the event date so the delay between the two is visible rather than hidden. NOT a deelzaak: an incident has no number, no term and no decision, and making one would give every report a beslistermijn it does not have (D-4).

widgets.title: Cards
widgets._note: leaf-integrations REQ-LEAF-105: a board for the ad-hoc coordination around a case, beside the tasks and never instead of them. NOTHING IN DOSSIQ READS OR WRITES A DECK CARD FROM A `task`, OR THE OTHER WAY ROUND. Task lifecycle belongs to WorkflowEngineService alone and the kanban WorkflowBoardView is the workflow surface; a mirror would give a handler two places to finish the same work and no rule about which one counts. A SECTION of the Work panel rather than a body widget with a layout entry, which is what the design named: the case body is a tab strip and its grid is full, and a card board is work, so it belongs beside the tasks. The leaf owns link, create and unlink, so dossiq ships no Deck code at all; with the Deck app absent the library renders its own empty state rather than an error.

widgets.title: Contacts
widgets._note: people-on-the-case: everyone involved in THIS case, read as OpenRegister person links rather than raw `role` rows. A person is a Nextcloud user or a contact, linked in one of the case schema's declared role types (SyncCaseRoleVocabulary writes them from the instance's role types), and PersonLinkListener projects the link onto a `role` record, so the resolver, the mandate matrix and the routing rules read what they always read. The contacts integration renders the people grouped by role type with avatar, email, validity window and note, and its picker offers users and contacts; the object-list this replaced showed a roleType uuid and a participant string nobody could act on.

widgets.title: Case parties
widgets._note: The party model OpenRegister shipped in #3761, which is the half the Parties section below cannot carry: a melder with no Nextcloud account, a gemachtigde acting for the applicant under Awb 2:1, an organisation naming a parent, and the indicators any of them hold. It reads GET /api/objects/{r}/{s}/{id}/parties, which answers the links grouped by role together with the kinds and roles the case schema declares, so a role renders under its label rather than under its key. The primary party is rendered first and its role group first, because the primary party is the one the case is filed against and a handler opening this tab is looking for that name before any other. TYPE names the registry key rather than "custom": a tab child renders through CnTabsWidget, which resolves cnRegistry[widget.type] and renders nothing at all, logging nothing, when no key answers. It sits BESIDE Parties and does not replace it: the contacts integration renders the person links people-on-the-case (#2683) writes, and a party with no account is invisible to it.

widgets.title: Seats
widgets._note: handing-a-case-over REQ-HAND-05. Two named seats: the handler doing the work and the coordinator answerable for it. The handler is `assignee` and stays so, because My Work, the queue and every lens already read it. The COORDINATOR IS NOT HERE, and that is the design rather than an omission: it is a role binding on the case (D-4), so it renders in Parties above with its role type beside every other person on the case. Putting a second copy of it here would be a second place to look and a second thing to keep in step. `hideEmpty` stays off: a case with no handler must show the row empty, because the absence is what a teamleider is looking for.

widgets.title: Followers
widgets._note: case-followers, row 13.18. Who is watching this case, over OpenRegister's GET /api/objects/{register}/{schema}/{id}/watchers (object-watchers). It sits LAST on this tab because the three sections above it say who the case is about and this one says who is reading over their shoulder: a teamleider following a sensitive case holds no role on it and appears here and nowhere else. TYPE names the registry key rather than "custom": a tab child resolves from cnRegistry[widget.type] and renders nothing at all, logging nothing, when no key answers. Reading the list needs `update` on the case, so a reader without it is told that in words rather than shown an empty list, which would be a claim about the audience nobody made to them. No remove button: taking off somebody else's subscription needs `manage`, and you stop following from the strip on the case page, which acts on your own row only.

widgets.title: Related cases
widgets._note: The Related cases tab, plus the follow-ups that do not exist yet (case-actions-menu row A26) and the series among them (planned-case-series, row 1.8). A series row carries its next occurrence, the cases it has already opened (filtered on `handoffSource` = `planned-series:<flowId>`, which every occurrence carries) and a Stop series action; stopping switches the flow off and leaves those cases alone. A planned follow-up is a SCHEDULED FLOW, not a case, and the `related` widget reads related OBJECTS, so it cannot list one; CasePlannedWidget wraps the library widget and hands it the planned rows as an extraSections group, leaving the built-in related content exactly as it was. The id, the title, the icon and the tab entry are all unchanged. TYPE is the registry key and NOT `custom`, because this is a child of the case-panels tabs widget: CnDetailPage renders a widget-<id> page slot per LAYOUT grid item only, a tab child is deliberately absent from layout, and CnTabsWidget resolves a tab child through cnRegistry[widget.type] and renders NOTHING at all when no key answers. Retyped back to `related` and this file deleted the day OpenRegister's related widget can include scheduled flows by subject (tasks 3.3). Waits on and blokkeert appear here with no section of their own: the pair is declared on the case schema as `x-openregister-relation-types`, and this widget groups by the label OpenRegister answers per direction. A hand-written section for either half would list the same links a second time, under a name this file chose rather than the one the schema did.

widgets.title: Sub-cases
widgets._note: deelzaak-support REQ 'Sub-cases section on parent case detail': 'The case detail view SHALL display a "Sub-cases" section ... listing all cases whose parentCase references the current case. The section MUST show each sub-case's title, status, assignee, and deadline.' Only the stats-block COUNT (case-kpis-sub-cases) existed; the listing lived on a separate route (/cases/:id/deelzaken, DeelzaakList), so the detail view had no such section and the requirement was unimplemented. The count widget already proves the filter shape works. Rows deep-link to CaseDetail because a sub-case IS a case.

widgets.title: Objects
widgets._note: The things a case is about: a building, a vehicle, a tree. `type` is `object-list` and not `custom` on purpose, because a tab child resolves by REGISTRY TYPE, so a `custom` widget named as a tab child renders nothing and logs nothing. Like its twelve siblings this widget is DELIBERATELY absent from `layout`: `case-panels` renders it, so a layout cell would render it twice. No `rowRoute`: a case object is a link row, not a record with a page of its own.
widgets._lensNote: The Object and Object status columns are LENSES, not stored fields. `objectTitle` and `objectStatus` are declared in `x-openregister-lenses` on the `caseObject` schema and resolved by OpenRegister on every read, so the tab shows what the linked object says about itself now rather than what somebody typed when they linked it. Nothing writes them: OpenRegister refuses a write that names a lens with a 400. They carry `widget: lensedValue` because an unreadable value arrives as `{"@withheld": true}`, an object, and the default cell would print `[object Object]`; a blank cell would be worse still, because blank reads as "there is no object". CnObjectListWidget forwards `widget` and `widgetProps` to CnCellRenderer, which resolves the name against the app's `cnCellWidgets`, so this needs no change in the library.

widgets.title: Programme
widgets._note: parties-and-contact-moments-consume-pipelinq 7.1, board DqZaakPartijen (the Programma card): the pipelinq programme this case hangs under, found by the work item that names it `dossiq:case`, with its progress and the mode that produced it, and the link dialog that shows pipelinq's refusal naming the holding programme. On the Related tab because a programme is a relation upward, like a parent case. Dossiq holds no programme and no budget. Rendered by TYPE (registry key case-programme).

The way from a case's objects to the schemas behind them (data-model-link, REQ-ADMIN-023). A SECTION and not a page-level `widgets[]` entry: a detail page carrying both spellings is the render-path shadowing gate-55 refuses. `nav-card-grid` resolves here because `registerCaseSections.js` adds it to the shared catalog, which is the only catalog CnDetailWidgetHost reads. Gated by `visibleIf` against `manifest.runtime.user.isAdmin`, not `permission`: CnNavCardGrid declares `permission` and reads it nowhere.
